children: companies delivered a largely positive earnings performance this week, with the majority beating analyst expectations on both earnings and revenue. However, year-over-year growth was more mixed, with six of the nine reporting companies posting increases in both EPS and sales.
Of the nine companies reporting this week, eight (89%) exceeded EPS expectations, while one fell short. Notably, six firms (67%) posted year-over-year EPS growth.
Of the nine companies reporting, seven (78%) exceeded revenue expectations, while two (22%) missed analyst estimates. Notably, six firms (67%) reported year-over-year revenue growth.
Here’s a look at some of the consumer discretionary firms that reported earnings this week:

beat on both the top- and bottom-line with 19% revenue growth and a profit of $3.16 per share coming in better than Wall Street expected. Gross booking value rose 21% to an above consensus $27.7B, while the average daily rate for a booking increased by 4% to $179, exceeding $177.14 estimates. Third quarter adjusted EBITDA improved by 19% to an above-consensus $2.5B.

reported an adjusted profit of $4.66 per share, up 17% year-over-year and 17 cents above expectations. Revenue was adjusted by $900M related to a matter associated with the Federal Trade Commission. Excluding this impact, revenue increased 9% to $9.8B, beating the consensus estimate of $9.54B.
reported a below consensus adjusted EPS of $0.33, with revenue falling 7.7% to $1.69B, which also missed estimates by $60M.

reported third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.56, which was above the $1.51 Bloomberg consensus. Revenue was $2.06B, compared with the $2.07B estimate. Growth at KFC helped offset weaker comparable sales at Taco Bell. KFC recorded 1% comparable-sales growth and a 6% increase in system sales excluding currency effects. Its reported operating profit rose 9% to $425M. Taco Bell's comparable sales fell 4%, and system sales declined 2%.
